problem: Visual navigation work assumes static scenes and cannot reason about how agent actions (e.g., pushing) change object poses, so agents fail when obstacles block the path or when an object must be pushed to a target.
motivation: Intelligent navigation sometimes requires interacting with the environment, e.g. pushing a chair out of the way. This needs long-horizon planning conditioned on the effects of agent-object and object-object interactions, which depend on object size, surroundings and applied force. The paper argues explicit action-outcome prediction is a crucial capability for embodied agents.
key_idea: A Neural Interaction Engine (NIE) predicts per-object, per-action affine transformations of 3D keypoints, and the resulting action-conditioned state features are fed to an RL policy trained jointly with a keypoint prediction loss.
insight: Explicitly predicting action effects, supervised only on the executed action, improves policy learning over plain PPO and over the CPC|A auxiliary loss. Removing visual input from NIE drops ObsNav SR from 80.0 to 72.7, because vision is needed to tell, e.g., that an object against a wall will not move. Both a lower (1x) and higher (10x) NIE loss weight hurt compared with alpha=3, so a balance between prediction and exploration is needed. Feeding keypoints alone without the NIE loss (RGB-D-K) helps only modestly, so the gain comes from the learned prediction.
method: Visual encoder: separate CNNs for RGB and depth (224x224) fused by a linear layer into v.
Keypoint extraction: Mask R-CNN segments objects (GT masks in training) and a heuristic detector picks 8 extreme-point corners per object, which depth and camera parameters back-project to 3D.

Affine transformation module: an MLP over keypoint, object-category and action embeddings predicts a 4x4 affine matrix per object and action; applying it to keypoints gives action-conditioned keypoints pa and preserves the rigid-body constraint.
State encoding and attention: keypoint centers c and ca are encoded, concatenated with category embeddings, and passed through self-attention over object categories plus average pooling to give ra.
Policy network: GRU-512 with actor and critic heads takes concat(goal g, v, ra) and is trained with PPO plus reward shaping (geodesic distance, +/-0.5 for opening/blocking a path in ObsNav).
NIE loss: L1 between predicted and GT action-conditioned keypoints, computed only for the executed action and observed object categories; total L = L_PPO + 3*L_NIE.

setting.backbone: Custom CNN visual encoder + NIE (MLP/self-attention) + GRU policy, trained from scratch with PPO; Mask R-CNN (ResNet-50 FPN) fine-tuned for segmentation
setting.training_data: Self-collected AI2-THOR datasets: 10k train / 2.5k val / 2.5k test episodes per task (ObsNav, ObjPlace); 20 object categories; Mask R-CNN pretrained on 8k images from training scenes; 10M PPO steps
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth (224x224) + GPS target coordinate (+ target object category for ObjPlace)
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveAhead 0.25 m, Rotate +/-90°, LookUp/Down 30°, Push/Pull/RightPush/LeftPush (100 N on the closest object), END
setting.simulator: AI2-iTHOR v2.7.2 (120 scenes: kitchens, living rooms, bedrooms, bathrooms), AllenAct
setting.privileged: GT object segmentation and GT object poses used during training only; at test time Mask R-CNN segmentation and a GPS target coordinate

numbers.extra: average of 3 runs; success radius 0.2 m; max 500 steps; unseen test scenes
average of 3 runs; target within 0.2 m; max 500 steps

numbers_note: Split is not labeled explicitly in the tables; the test set is described as 2.5k instances from 5 test scenes per room category.
results: On ObsNav, NIE reaches 80.0% SR versus 73.8% for the strongest baseline (CPC|A) and 67.1% for PPO. On ObjPlace, NIE reaches 17.5% SR versus 12.0% for CPC|A, while PPO, RGB-D-S and RGB-D-K stay near 1%.
limitations: Absolute ObjPlace success is low (17.5%), and baselines often push other objects and block the path.
Relies on a heuristic corner keypoint detector and a Mask R-CNN (47.4 AP), with only rigid-body pushes in simulation on 20 object categories.
Requires ground-truth object poses and segmentation for training and careful reward shaping (the path-open/blocked reward is essential for ObsNav).
